title: A punctured normal curve realizing a prescribed finite generic field extension
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Let $T$ be an integral affine scheme of finite type over $k$, with generic point $\eta$, and let $y\in T$ be a closed point satisfying $\dim\mathcal O_{T,y}=1$ [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Put $K=\kappa(\eta)$ [def-weil-residue-field] and let $L/K$ be any finite field extension. Let $Y$ and $W$ be schemes locally of finite type over $k$, let $i:T\to Y$ and $f:W\to Y$ be $k$-morphisms, and let $u:\operatorname{Spec}L\to W$ be a $k$-morphism such that $fu$ equals $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}K\to T\xrightarrow{i}Y$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-pc-scheme-fibre]. There exist an integral scheme $C$ of finite type over $k$, a $k$-morphism $p:C\to T$, a closed point $c\in C$, and a $k$-morphism $a:C\setminus\{c\}\to W$ such that every local ring of $C$ is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], $p(c)=y$, $\dim\mathcal O_{C,c}=1$, and $fa=i p$ on $C\setminus\{c\}$. Moreover there is an identification $\kappa(\eta_C)=L$ respecting $K$, under which the generic restriction of $p$ is the specified map $\operatorname{Spec}L\to T$ and the generic restriction of $a$ is exactly $u$. No separability hypothesis on $L/K$ and no separatedness hypothesis on $W$ or $Y$ is imposed.

Uses Morphisms Tag 0BX8 (morphisms-lemma-rational-map-finite-presentation) for spreading the generic map.

proof.text: Write $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$, where $A$ is a finitely generated $k$-algebra and a domain. By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction], the given $K=\kappa(\eta)$ is the fraction field of $A$. Form $B=\overline A^{\,L}\subset L$ and $N=\operatorname{Spec}B$, with $p_N:N\to T$, as in [def-fin-normalization-extension]. This is also the relative normalization of $T$ in $\operatorname{Spec}L$ of [lem-weil-pbc-relative-normalization]: by its clause (iii) for the affine open $U=T$, its ring of global sections is the integral closure of $A$ in $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}L,\mathcal O)=L$, which is $B$, compatibly with $A\to B\subset L$. The map $\operatorname{Spec}L\to T$ is affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Its source is integral with local ring the field $L$, which is integrally closed. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-normalization-normal-stalks] makes every local ring of $N$ an integrally closed domain. Also $B$ is a nonzero subring of $L$, so $N$ is integral. By [lem-fin-normalization-extension-finite] and [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], $B$ is a finite $A$-module.

source.place: Tag 0GWV, limits-lemma-essentially-finite-type-criterion-universally-closed, final paragraph of proof (normalization and punctured representative); explicit affine-curve version of the shrinking argument.

proof.text: Choose finite $k$-algebra generators of $A$ and finite $A$-module generators of $B$. Together their images generate $B$ as a $k$-algebra: every element of $B$ is an $A$-linear combination of the chosen module generators. Hence $N$ is affine of finite type over $k$. The closed point $y$ corresponds to a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $A$; [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-domain-dimension-local-ring] gives $\dim A=\dim A_{\mathfrak m}=1$. The inclusion $A\hookrightarrow B$ is integral by the construction of $B$, so [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-dimension-equal] gives $\dim B=1$. Moreover [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components] shows that $N$ is Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 0GWV, limits-lemma-essentially-finite-type-criterion-universally-closed, final paragraph of proof (normalization and punctured representative); explicit affine-curve version of the shrinking argument.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-lying-over], choose $\mathfrak n\subset B$ over $\mathfrak m$. It is maximal by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-prime-over-maximal-maximal], and therefore defines a closed point $c\in N$ with $p_N(c)=y$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-domain-dimension-local-ring] to the finitely generated $k$-domain $B$ gives $\dim\mathcal O_{N,c}=\dim B=1$. By [lem-sbc-normalization-generic-field], identify the function field of $N$ with the prescribed $L$, with the canonical generic map $\operatorname{Spec}L\to N$ and its composition with $p_N$ agreeing with the specified map to $T$. In particular this identification respects $K$.

source.place: Tag 0GWV, limits-lemma-essentially-finite-type-criterion-universally-closed, final paragraph of proof (normalization and punctured representative); explicit affine-curve version of the shrinking argument.

proof.text: The morphism $f:W\to Y$ is locally of finite type. Indeed, take any affine opens $V\subseteq Y$ and $D\subseteq W$ with $f(D)\subseteq V$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] to $W\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ shows that $\mathcal O_W(D)$ is finitely generated over $k$. The same generators generate it over $\mathcal O_Y(V)$, since the composite $k\to\mathcal O_Y(V)\to\mathcal O_W(D)$ is its given $k$-algebra structure. The reverse direction of that same criterion now proves the assertion about $f$.

source.place: Tag 0GWV, limits-lemma-essentially-finite-type-criterion-universally-closed, final paragraph of proof (normalization and punctured representative); explicit affine-curve version of the shrinking argument.

proof.text: By Step 2, $N=\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B$ Noetherian, so $N$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] (the one-member affine cover). Let $\eta_N$ be its generic point; $\mathcal O_{N,\eta_N}$ is the function field of $N$. By Step 3 there is an isomorphism $e:\operatorname{Spec}L\cong\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{N,\eta_N}$ such that the canonical map $\alpha:\operatorname{Spec}L\to N$ is $c_{\eta_N}\circ e$, where $c_{\eta_N}$ is the canonical morphism, and $p_N\alpha$ is the specified map $\operatorname{Spec}L\to T$. Apply [lem-sfb-local-ring-map-spread] with $S=Y$, $T=N$, $a=i p_N$, $Z=W$, $g=f$ (locally of finite type by Step 4), $t=\eta_N$ and $\varphi=u\circ e^{-1}$. Its hypothesis holds: $f\varphi=fue^{-1}=ip_N\alpha e^{-1}=ip_Nc_{\eta_N}$, using the assumption that $fu$ is $\operatorname{Spec}L\to T\xrightarrow{i}Y$. Obtain an open $V\subseteq N$ containing $\eta_N$ and $b:V\to W$ with $fb=ip_N|_V$ and $b\circ c_{\eta_N,V}=\varphi$, i.e. $b$ composed with the generic map $\operatorname{Spec}L\to V$ of Step 3 is exactly $u$. This is a $k$-morphism: compose $fb=ip_N|_V$ with $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and use that $f,i,p_N$ are $k$-morphisms.

source.place: Tag 0GWV, limits-lemma-essentially-finite-type-criterion-universally-closed, final paragraph of proof (normalization and punctured representative); explicit affine-curve version of the shrinking argument.

proof.text: Replace $V$ by $V\setminus\{c\}$ and restrict $b$. It still contains the generic point since $\dim\mathcal O_{N,c}=1$. Put $E=N\setminus V$, a proper closed subset containing $c$. By [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components] it has finitely many irreducible components, and [lem-sc-scheme-sober] gives a generic point for each. Such a generic point corresponds to a nonzero prime of the domain $B$, since $E$ excludes the generic point of $N$. Every nonzero prime of $B$ is maximal: otherwise $0\subsetneq\mathfrak p\subsetneq\mathfrak q$ would contradict $\dim B=1$. Thus each component is a single closed point. It follows that $\Sigma=E\setminus\{c\}$ is a finite set of closed points disjoint from $c$. For each $z\in\Sigma$ choose $s_z\in\mathfrak m_z\setminus\mathfrak n$, possible because the two maximal ideals are distinct, and put $s=\prod_zs_z$ (the empty product is $1$). Then $s\notin\mathfrak n$ and $s\in\mathfrak m_z$ for all $z\in\Sigma$. Consequently $C=D(s)\subseteq N$ contains $c$, avoids $\Sigma$, and satisfies $C\setminus\{c\}\subseteq V$.

source.place: Tag 0GWV, limits-lemma-essentially-finite-type-criterion-universally-closed, final paragraph of proof (normalization and punctured representative); explicit affine-curve version of the shrinking argument.

proof.text: Take $p=p_N|_C$ and $a=b|_{C\setminus\{c\}}$. Since $s\notin\mathfrak n$, $C=\operatorname{Spec}B_s$ is nonempty and integral, and $B_s=B[t]/(st-1)$ is finitely generated over $k$. Thus $C$ is of finite type over $k$. By the open-subscheme identification of [def-weil-open-immersion], local rings on $C$ are the same as those on $N$; hence they are integrally closed domains and $\dim\mathcal O_{C,c}=1$. The point $c$ stays closed and $p(c)=y$. The generic point belongs to $C$, its local ring is unchanged, and the identification with $L$ from Step 3 still respects $K$. All generic restrictions are therefore the prescribed ones, in particular $a|_{\operatorname{Spec}L}=u$. Restricting the equality in Step 5 gives $fa=ip$.
